title: The twisting sheaf O(1) on P^n_Z on the standard charts
statement: Let $n\ge0$, $S=\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$ graded by total degree, $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj] with standard opens $D_+(T_j)$ and $\Gamma(D_+(f),\mathcal O)=S_{(f)}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ the $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-module attached to the shifted graded module $S(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (so $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(f))=S(1)_{(f)}=(S_f)_1$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree), with the global sections $T_0,\dots,T_n\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},\mathcal O(1))$ given by $T_l\mapsto T_l/1\in(S_f)_1$ on every $D_+(f)$. Then: (i) $\mathcal O(1)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]; more precisely, for every $j$ the map $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}\to\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}$, $a\mapsto a\cdot T_j|$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}$-modules, and the $D_+(T_j)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$; (ii) for every $j$, $D_+(T_j)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$ and $S_{(T_j)}=\mathbf Z[T_0/T_j,\dots,T_n/T_j]$ is the polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in the $n$ elements $T_l/T_j$, $l\neq j$; (iii) $D_+(T_j)$ is the non-vanishing locus $(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})_{T_j}=\{x: T_{j,x}\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal O(1)_x\}$ of the section $T_j$ ($\mathfrak m_x$ the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},x}$ [def-weil-residue-field]); (iv) for all $j,l$, $T_l|_{D_+(T_j)}=(T_l/T_j)\cdot T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ in $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(T_j))$, where $T_l/T_j\in S_{(T_j)}=\Gamma(D_+(T_j),\mathcal O)$; (v) $\mathcal O(1)$ is canonically the glued module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] for $A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$: if $\mathcal L$ is that module, with bases $e_j$ of $\mathcal L|_{D_+(T_j)}$ and $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ on $D_+(T_i)\cap D_+(T_j)$, there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}$-modules $\Phi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal O(1)$ with $\Phi(e_j)=T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$ for all $j$, and $\Phi$ carries the global section $x_l$ of $\mathcal L$ given by $(T_l/T_j)e_j$ on each $D_+(T_j)$ to $T_l$.

proof.text: *(ii) and the cover.* Every homogeneous element of $S$ of positive degree is a $\mathbf Z$-combination of monomials of positive degree, each divisible by some $T_l$; so $T_0,\dots,T_n$ generate the irrelevant ideal $S_+$, and the standard opens $D_+(T_0),\dots,D_+(T_n)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. Each $T_j$ is homogeneous of degree $1>0$, so $D_+(T_j)$ is an open subscheme with a canonical isomorphism $D_+(T_j)\cong\operatorname{Spec}S_{(T_j)}$, under which $\Gamma(D_+(T_j),\mathcal O)=S_{(T_j)}$ [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dehomogenization-polynomial-ring] with $A=\mathbf Z$, $S_{(T_j)}=\mathbf Z[T_l/T_j:l\neq j]$ is the polynomial ring over $\mathbf Z$ in the $n$ elements $T_l/T_j$. This is (ii) and the last clause of (i).

proof.text: *$\mathcal O(1)$ on the standard opens.* By the definition of $\mathcal O(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (a),(b),(d): for $g\in S$ homogeneous of positive degree, $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(g))=S(1)_{(g)}=(S_g)_1$, the fractions $a/g^m$ with $a\in S_{m\deg g+1}$, a module over $\mathcal O(D_+(g))=S_{(g)}$ by multiplication in $S_g$; for $D_+(h)\subseteq D_+(g)$ the restriction $(S_g)_1\to(S_h)_1$ is the canonical localization map, which is compatible with multiplication by elements of $S_{(g)}$; and the global section $T_l$ (the image of $T_l\in S_1=S(1)_0$) restricts to $T_l/1\in(S_g)_1$ on every $D_+(g)$.

*$T_j$ trivializes $\mathcal O(1)$ on $D_+(T_j)$ (Stacks 01MS with $d=1$, $n=1$).* Let $g$ be homogeneous of positive degree with $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(T_j)$. Then $g^e=aT_j$ for some $e\ge1$ and homogeneous $a$ [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (a), so $T_j/1$ is a unit of $S_g$ (inverse $a/g^e$). Hence $\beta_g:S_{(g)}\to(S_g)_1$, $b\mapsto b\cdot(T_j/1)$, is bijective: it is injective because $T_j/1$ is a unit of $S_g$; and for $c\in(S_g)_1$ the element $b=c\cdot(T_j/1)^{-1}\in S_g$ is homogeneous of degree $1-1=0$ (product of homogeneous elements of degrees $1$ and $-1$), so $b\in(S_g)_0=S_{(g)}$ and $\beta_g(b)=c$. Now let $\mu_j:\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}\to\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}$, $a\mapsto a\cdot T_j|$, a morphism of $\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}$-modules (it is linear on each open, and $(a\,T_j|_V)|_W=a|_W\,T_j|_W$). By step 2 its component on $D_+(g)$ is $\beta_g$, hence bijective. The opens $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(T_j)$ form a basis of the topology of $D_+(T_j)$ (the $D_+(g)$ form a basis of the topology of $\operatorname{Proj}$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], and $D_+(g)\cap D_+(T_j)=D_+(gT_j)$), so for $x\in D_+(T_j)$ the stalks of $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal O(1)$ at $x$ are the colimits over the cofinal system of these $D_+(g)\ni x$, and the stalk map $\mu_{j,x}$, a colimit of bijections, is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks], $\mu_j$ is an isomorphism. In particular, for every open $V\subseteq D_+(T_j)$ each $t\in\mathcal O(1)(V)$ is $a\cdot T_j|_V$ for exactly one $a\in\mathcal O(V)$, and for $x\in D_+(T_j)$ the stalk $\mathcal O(1)_x$ is free of rank one over $\mathcal O_x$ with basis $T_{j,x}$.

proof.text: *(i).* By step 1 the $D_+(T_j)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, and by step 3 $\mathcal O(1)|_{D_+(T_j)}\cong\mathcal O_{D_+(T_j)}$ via $\mu_j$. So $\mathcal O(1)$ is locally free of rank one; it is quasi-coherent ([lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (c), or because it is locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf). Hence $\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], and the isomorphisms $\mu_j$ are the ones claimed in (i).

source.place: Lemma 01MT (label lemma-apply-modules): $X$ covered by $D_+(f)$, $f\in S_1$, so $\mathcal O_X(n)$ is invertible

proof.text: *(iv).* In $\mathcal O(1)(D_+(T_j))=(S_{T_j})_1$ (step 2), $T_l|_{D_+(T_j)}=T_l/1$ and $T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}=T_j/1$, and the $\mathcal O(D_+(T_j))=S_{(T_j)}$-module structure is multiplication in $S_{T_j}$. Since $(T_l/T_j)\cdot(T_j/1)=T_lT_j/T_j=T_l/1$ in $S_{T_j}$, with $T_l/T_j\in S_{(T_j)}$ (degree $0$), we get $T_l|_{D_+(T_j)}=(T_l/T_j)\cdot T_j|_{D_+(T_j)}$. (For $l=j$, $T_j/T_j=1$.)

*(iii) (Stacks 01MV with $d=1$).* Let $Z=\{x:T_{j,x}\notin\mathfrak m_x\mathcal O(1)_x\}$. Fix $k$ and $x\in D_+(T_k)$. By step 3 (for $k$), $\mathcal O_x\to\mathcal O(1)_x$, $a\mapsto a\,T_{k,x}$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_x$-modules; it carries $\mathfrak m_x$ onto $\mathfrak m_x\mathcal O(1)_x$. By (iv) (step 5, for $k$), $T_{j,x}=(T_j/T_k)_x\,T_{k,x}$, the image of the germ $(T_j/T_k)_x$ of the function $T_j/T_k\in S_{(T_k)}=\Gamma(D_+(T_k),\mathcal O)$. Hence $x\in Z$ iff $(T_j/T_k)_x\notin\mathfrak m_x$ iff $x\in D(T_j/T_k)$, the basic open of the function $T_j/T_k$ on the scheme $D_+(T_k)$ [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] ($\mathcal O_x$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field]). By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] with $f=T_k$, $g=T_j$, $d=e=1$, $D(T_j/T_k)=D_+(T_k)\cap D_+(T_j)$. So $Z\cap D_+(T_k)=D_+(T_j)\cap D_+(T_k)$ for every $k$, and since the $D_+(T_k)$ cover $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ (step 1), $Z=D_+(T_j)$.

proof.text: *(v) The glued module is $\mathcal O(1)$.* Let $\mathcal L$ be the module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] for $A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$, $U_j=D_+(T_j)$: it comes with isomorphisms $\mathcal O_{U_j}\cong\mathcal L|_{U_j}$, $1\mapsto e_j$, and $e_i=(T_i/T_j)e_j$ on $U_i\cap U_j$. Define $\Phi_j:\mathcal L|_{U_j}\to\mathcal O(1)|_{U_j}$, $a\,e_j\mapsto a\,T_j|$, i.e. $\mu_j$ of step 3 composed with the inverse of $1\mapsto e_j$; it is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U_j}$-modules. On $U_i\cap U_j$: $\Phi_j(e_i)=\Phi_j((T_i/T_j)e_j)=(T_i/T_j)T_j=T_i=\Phi_i(e_i)$ by (iv) restricted to $U_i\cap U_j$; as $e_i$ is a basis of $\mathcal L$ on $U_i\cap U_j$ and both maps are $\mathcal O$-linear, $\Phi_i=\Phi_j$ there. Morphisms of $\mathcal O$-modules form a sheaf $\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal L,\mathcal O(1))$ [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-is-sheaf], so the $\Phi_j$ glue to a unique $\Phi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal O(1)$ with $\Phi|_{U_j}=\Phi_j$; likewise the inverses $\Phi_j^{-1}$ (compatible for the same reason) glue to $\Psi:\mathcal O(1)\to\mathcal L$, and $\Psi\Phi$, $\Phi\Psi$ restrict to identities on every $U_j$, hence are identities: $\Phi$ is an isomorphism with $\Phi(e_j)=T_j|_{U_j}$. Uniqueness: any $\Phi'$ with $\Phi'(e_j)=T_j|_{U_j}$ agrees with $\Phi_j$ on $U_j$ (both $\mathcal O$-linear, $e_j$ a basis), so $\Phi'=\Phi$ by the sheaf property of $\mathcal{H}om$. Sections: the local sections $(T_l/T_j)e_j$ on $U_j$ agree on overlaps, since $(T_l/T_i)e_i=(T_l/T_i)(T_i/T_j)e_j=(T_l/T_j)e_j$ by the identity $(T_l/T_i)(T_i/T_j)=T_l/T_j$ in $S_{(T_iT_j)}=\mathcal O(U_i\cap U_j)$ (restriction maps of $\mathcal O$ are the localization maps, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (b) with $M=S$), so they glue to $x_l\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z},\mathcal L)$; and $\Phi(x_l)|_{U_j}=(T_l/T_j)T_j|_{U_j}=T_l|_{U_j}$ by (iv), so $\Phi(x_l)=T_l$ since the $U_j$ cover (step 1).
